newsitem.title: CHINA: China raises ex-refinery kerosene price by $17.5.
newsitem.headline: China raises ex-refinery kerosene price by $17.5.

text.p: China has raised its state-set ex-refinery kerosene price by 145 yuan ($17.5) per tonne from July 1, an official of the State Planning Commission said on Tuesday.
The ex-refinery kerosene price before the increase was 2,055 yuan per tonne for most parts of China except in several remote provinces, the official said.
"The price increase was aimed to reduce price differences between kerosene and other oil products," the official said.
The kerosene ex-refinery price in northwestern Xinjiang region was raised to 2,025 yuan per tonne from 1,880 yuan from July 1, he said.
Price in northwestern Gansu and Qinghai provinces was raised to 2,105 yuan per tonne from 1,960 yuan.
The ex-refinery price of kerosene used for jet fuel remained unchanged at about 2,230 yuan per tonne, the official said without giving further details.
